### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
🚨 **BLOCKING**: _none_ — see 💡 suggestions below.

💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicate `latestDispatchedVerdict` probe + "fail closed" wording precision**

In the moved-head path (`headMovedCleanVf`), `latestDispatchedVerdict(...)` is called with the exact same arguments (`effectiveRepoInfo`, same resolved workflow, `uHead`) that `headChangedNoVerdictVf` (line ~1426) already used. On a parked machine PR with a park comment and a non-green rollup, that is two identical `gh api .../runs?head_sha=` probes in the same tick. Hoisting the verdict into one shared local would halve it:

```javascript
var headVerdictVf = latestDispatchedVerdict(effectiveRepoInfo,
    rule.ciWorkflow || ((RUN_JOB_PARAMS || {}).ciWorkflow) || 'quality.yml', uHead);
var headChangedNoVerdictVf = !!uHead && parkedHeadVf !== null &&
    parkedHeadVf !== '' && uHead !== parkedHeadVf &&
    headVerdictVf !== 'failure';
// ...
headMovedCleanVf = !isNaN(headTsVf) && !isNaN(parkedTsVf) &&
    headTsVf > parkedTsVf && headVerdictVf !== 'failure';
```

Also note: the new comment (lines 1434–1436) says "both probes fail closed themselves" — true for `parkResetCommit`/`parkedSince` (null-guarded) and `validationRollupGreen`/`headCommitActor` (error → false/NaN), but `latestDispatchedVerdict` **fails open** in this context: a probe error returns `null`, and `null !== 'failure'` lets the moved-head clear proceed. That is inherited #633 semantics and self-heals within one CI cycle (a genuinely red head is re-discovered by validation), but since these comments are the institutional memory of this ladder, worth an explicit "(verdict probe fails open — same as #633; re-validation re-discovers red)" caveat.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
💡 **SUGGESTION: machine self-clear comment carries no audit evidence (no head sha, no park time)**

The #633 clear comment cites both shas (parked head vs current head), and the human-push comment cites actor + date. The new machine clear comment posts only a fixed narrative:

```javascript
body: '🅿️→▶ validation_failed cleared — this MACHINE-authored PR was ' +
    'parked with no self-clear path (the machine pushes its own heads, so ' +
    'the human-push reset can never fire): ' + machineUnparkWhyVf + '. ' + ...
```

`machineUnparkWhyVf` states the *reason class* ("head moved past the park...") but not the evidence. For the moved-head branch, including the head sha/date and the park time would make the decision auditable directly from the PR thread — the same convention the two sibling branches follow, and valuable when someone later asks "why did the park vanish on <date>":

```javascript
'...the head moved past the park carrying no red verdict of its own ' +
'(head `' + uHead.slice(0, 8) + '` @ ' + headActorVf.date +
' > park ' + parkedAtVf + '). '
```

Trivial to add — `headActorVf`/`parkedAtVf` are already in scope.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
💡 **SUGGESTION: this is the third near-identical copy of the clear-block — extract a `clearPark(...)` helper**

The ladder now has three structurally identical branches (`headChangedNoVerdictVf` #633, the new `machineUnparkVf` gh-750, and the human-push RESET), plus a fourth variant in `validate_pr`'s park backstop (~line 1630): each does `!DRY` → `github_remove_label` → try/catch warn → `github_create_comment` → try/catch warn → console.log → `unparkedThisPass = true`. The new branch copies the pattern faithfully (✅ DRY-guarded, ✅ both writes independently try/catch'd), but the ladder has now paid the copy cost three times — the next park fix will make it four.

A small local helper inside `processRule` would collapse each branch to one line and guarantee the DRY guard / error handling stay uniform:

```javascript
function clearParkAndSay(whyBody, logLine) {
    if (!DRY) {
        try {
            github_remove_label({ workspace: effectiveRepoInfo.owner,
```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instruction…

Limit 20 (owner 2026-09-22): silent pushes fire no CI — refreshing every BEHIND head every tick is free and keeps PRs merge-ready, so the merge window never waits for a refresh first. STICKY PARK (owner 2026-09-27, live: fa#923): before refreshing, a GUEST PR whose current head has RED checks is labeled validation_failed (idempotent, the head SHA noted in a one-time comment) — validate-armed excludes the label and no validation CI is dispatched for it at all; the label is REMOVED only when the LAST SUBSTANTIVE commit (machine-authored merges of main walked back past, dmtools-agents#681) is a NON-machine push NEWER than the park, so the SM's own silent-updates — bot merges or re-arms — never clear a red guest's park. Machine-authored PRs never get the label (fa pushes their heads). MACHINE SELF-CLEAR (gh-750, owner directive 2026-10-05): a MACHINE-authored parked PR — legacy residue like fa#1227, the label predates this guest-only contract — clears when the current head's check rollup is GREEN or the head moved past the park carrying no red verdict of its own (probe failures keep the park, fail closed); guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior.",

This rule routes every parked non-validating PR through update_branch's RESET probe regardless of merge state: a NON-machine SUBSTANTIVE push NEWER than the newest park event clears the label — the probe walks back past machine-authored merges of main to the last substantive commit: a bot merge BURIES the retrigger, never replaces it (dmtools-agents#681, live fa#1213 2026-10-03 22:56–23:10: retrigger 7ecf11d7 buried by bot merge b3f9c6b5 before the next tick, the old head-keyed probe declined and the park survived 4 real ticks); then validate-armed picks the PR up on a later pass (this rule never dispatches CI itself); machine pushes and stale heads keep the park (fail closed). # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 752
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/752
- **Title**: gh-750 Machine PR + validation_failed = permanent park: no self-clear path (live: fa #1227)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-750` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +268
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T18:48:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T19:04:40Z

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

Limit 20 (owner 2026-09-22): silent pushes fire no CI — refreshing every BEHIND head every tick is free and keeps PRs merge-ready, so the merge window never waits for a refresh first. STICKY PARK (owner 2026-09-27, live: fa#923): before refreshing, a GUEST PR whose current head has RED checks is labeled validation_failed (idempotent, the head SHA noted in a one-time comment) — validate-armed excludes the label and no validation CI is dispatched for it at all; the label is REMOVED only when the LAST SUBSTANTIVE commit (machine-authored merges of main walked back past, dmtools-agents#681) is a NON-machine push NEWER than the park, so the SM's own silent-updates — bot merges or re-arms — never clear a red guest's park. Machine-authored PRs never get the label (fa pushes their heads). This rule routes every parked non-validating PR through update_branch's RESET probe regardless of merge state: a NON-machine SUBSTANTIVE push NEWER than the newest park event clears the label — the probe walks back past machine-authored merges of main to the last substantive commit: a bot merge BURIES the retrigger, never replaces it (dmtools-agents#681, live fa#1213 2026-10-03 22:56–23:10: retrigger 7ecf11d7 buried by bot merge b3f9c6b5 before the next tick, the old head-keyed probe declined and the park survived 4 real ticks); then validate-armed picks the PR up on a later pass (this rule never dispatches CI itself); machine pushes and stale heads keep the park (fail closed). The silent branch refresh inside the action is a no-op for a non-BEHIND head (git merge reports up-to-date, no push). MACHINE SELF-CLEAR (gh-750, owner directive 2026-10-05, live fa#1227): this rule is the ONLY exit a MACHINE-authored parked PR will ever get — fa pushes their own heads, so the non-machine substantive push never lands, the #633 park-comment sha is missing on legacy parks, and the rework armers list validation_failed as an in-flight blocker so no rework leg fires (#1227: pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + MERGEABLE, parked since the CI-storm era).       - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 752
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/752
- **Title**: gh-750 Machine PR + validation_failed = permanent park: no self-clear path (live: fa #1227)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-750` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +268
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T18:48:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T19:04:40Z

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

Due to short-circuit `&&`, the probe runs only if `uHead` is truthy AND `parkedHeadVf` is non-null and non-empty AND differs from uHead. So in the current code, the first probe is conditional on park-comment sha known + different. The second probe runs when machine PR && !greenRollupVf (and uHead, actorVf, parkedAtVf non-null).

- Machine PR, park comment missing (legacy parks — the gh-750 case): first probe short-circuits (parkedHeadVf === null), so only the second probe runs → currently 1 probe in the moved-head path. Hoisting an unconditional probe would keep it 1 probe.

Hmm. That changes probe behavior for guests: guest + no park comment → currently 0 verdict probes, after unconditional hoist → 1 probe per tick. That's a regression in probe economy for guests.


```js
var headChangedNoVerdictVf = !!uHead && parkedHeadVf !== null && ... && headVerdictVf !== 'failure';
```

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 752
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/752
- **Title**: gh-750 Machine PR + validation_failed = permanent park: no self-clear path (live: fa #1227)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-750` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +268
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T18:48:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T19:04:40Z

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instruction…

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```

7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.


# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# PR #752 Rework — review threads addressed (commit `42f1f9f8`)

## Issues/Notes

All 4 open threads were 💡 suggestion-level (0 🚨 blocking, 0 ⚠️ important — matching the review verdict). Three fixed, one deferred per the reviewer's own guidance:

| Thread | Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (`js/smAgent.js`) | duplicate `latestDispatchedVerdict` probe + "fail closed" wording imprecision | ✅ **Fixed** — shared memoized probe + fail-open caveat documented |
| 2 (`js/smAgent.js`) | machine clear comment carries no audit evidence | ✅ **Fixed** — head sha @ commit date > park time now cited |
| 3 (`js/smAgent.js`) | third copy of the clear-block → extract `clearPark(...)` helper | ⏸️ **Deferred to follow-up** — reviewer: "pure refactor… fine to defer"; spans pre-existing #633 / human-push / `validate_pr` branches outside gh-750 scope |
| 4 (`sm_github.json`) | "ONLY exit" exclusivity claim imprecise | ✅ **Fixed** — both description tweaks applied as suggested |

No CI failures were present; no merge conflicts.

## Approach

TDD (RED → GREEN) per finding — each fix landed with a test that failed first against the pre-fix code:

1. **Probe hoist (thread 1):** replaced the two identical `latestDispatchedVerdict(effectiveRepoInfo, <resolved ciWorkflow>, uHead)` calls with one memoized local, `probeHeadVerdictVf()` — a `var` function expression (GraalJS-safe) that probes at most once per tick. The memoized form (vs a bare unconditional hoist) keeps the existing short-circuits: no path *gains* a probe — the #633 consumer fires only when the park-comment sha is known and differs, the machine consumer only when the rollup isn't green. The sticky-park comment now states explicitly that the dispatched-verdict probe **fails open** for the clear decision (error → null → "no red", inherited #633 semantics; re-validation re-discovers red) while `parkResetCommit`/`parkedSince`/`validationRollupGreen`/`headCommitActor` fail closed.
2. **Audit evidence (thread 2):** the moved-head branch of `machineUnparkWhyVf` now reads `…carrying no red verdict of its own (head `<sha8>` @ <commit date> > park <park time>)`; the reason rides both the PR clear comment and the tick log. `headActorVf`/`parkedAtVf` were already in scope; guarded defensively.
3. **Docs (thread 4):** `park-reset` description now scopes the exclusivity claim ("a MACHINE-authored parked PR's only exit **when the head is NOT BEHIND** — silent-update-behind serves BEHIND heads through the same shared RESET probe"); `silent-update-behind` now notes the label's SET rules are **guest-gated** (legacy parks predate that). Rule queries/code untouched.
4. **Helper extraction (thread 3):** deferred — see `outputs/review_replies/thread_3.md`.

## Files Modified

- `js/smAgent.js` — shared memoized verdict probe (`probeHeadVerdictVf`) in the `update_branch` sticky-park ladder; fail-open caveat in the gh-750 block comment; audit evidence in `machineUnparkWhyVf` (moved-head branch). Ladder order, gating, and fail-closed posture unchanged.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 3 new tests in the sticky-park suite (details below).
- `sm_github.json` — `park-reset` + `silent-update-behind` description precision only (still valid JSON).

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}

    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}

    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>
